headline: Treasury drops its crypto mixer and self-custody wallet rules

scenes.vo: The Treasury Department just pulled two crypto surveillance proposals that hung over the industry for years. Here's what changed.
Its financial crimes unit withdrew a twenty twenty rule on self-custody wallets and a twenty twenty-three plan targeting crypto mixers. It said the mixer rule could chill legitimate activity.
Here's why traders are watching it. The wallet rule would have made exchanges log and report transfers to self-custody wallets over three thousand dollars. That's now off the table.
The catch. Withdrawing a proposal isn't a green light. Money laundering and sanctions laws still apply, and a new rule could return.
Here's what happens next. Watch for the Federal Register notices this week, and whether Congress takes this up in market structure talks.
